title: Therapeutic Gene Delivery and Transfection in Human Pancreatic Cancer Cells using Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor-targeted Gelatin Nanoparticles
protocol: Synthesize thiolated gelatin by covalently conjugating type B gelatin with 2-iminothiolane.
Dissolve 1 gram of gelatin in 100 ml deionized water and incubate with 20 mg 2-iminothiolane hydrochloride at room temperature for 15 hours.
Remove unreacted reagent by dialysis against 5 mM HCl solution, followed by 1 mM HCl solution for 3 hours each.
Purify thiolated gelatin and freeze dry it for storage at 4°C.
Dissolve 200 mg thiolated gelatin in water and adjust pH to 7 with 0.2 M NaOH solution.
Add 1 mg DNA to the gelatin solution and gently mix.
Slowly add chilled ethanol to the mixture while stirring at high speed until nanoparticles form when solvent composition changes to 75% hydro-alcoholic solution.
Crosslink nanoparticles by adding 0.1 ml of 8% (v/v) glyoxal solution slowly.
Quench unreacted reagents with 0.5 ml of 0.2 M glycine solution.
Ultra-centrifuge the nanoparticles at 16,000 rpm for 30 minutes.
Wash pellets twice with deionized water and freeze-dry purified nanoparticles for storage at 4°C.
Suspend nanoparticles in 0.1 M phosphate buffer (pH 7.4) at a concentration of 10 mg/ml.
Incubate nanoparticles with 2 times weight of methoxy-PEG-succinimidyl carboxy methyl ester (mPEG-SCM, MW 2,000 Da) for 2 hours at room temperature with slow stirring.
Collect PEGylated nanoparticles by ultra-centrifugation at 16,000 rpm for 30 minutes.
Wash pellets with deionized water twice.
Freeze-dry purified nanoparticles and store them at 4°C.
Suspend MAL-PEG-SCM modified nanoparticles in 0.1 M phosphate buffer (pH 6.5) at a concentration of 10 mg/ml.
Incubate nanoparticles with 10% weight of EGFR specific peptide (Y-H-W-Y-G-Y-T-P-Q-N-V-I-G-G-G-G-C) for 6 hours at room temperature with slow stirring.
Collect peptide modified nanoparticles by ultra-centrifugation at 16,000 rpm for 30 minutes.
Wash pellets with deionized water twice.
Freeze-dry purified nanoparticles and store them at 4°C.
Mount lyophilized nanoparticles on an aluminum sample mount.
Sputter-coat the samples with palladium to enhance conductivity and minimize charge buildup.
Observe the surface morphology of the samples under a Hitachi 4800 field emission scanning electron microscope at 3 kV.
Digest nanoparticles with 0.2 mg/ml protease in PBS (30 min at 37°C).
Digest nanoparticles with 0.2 U/ml DNAse (10 min at room temperature).
Load samples onto 1.2% agarose gel at a concentration of 100 ng/well in a 18 μL volume per well.
Run the gel at 75 V for 30 minutes.
Use Kodak Digital X-ray Specimen System to visualize bands with UV transluminescence.
Suspend nanoparticles containing plasmid DNA at 1 mg/ml and digest them with 0.2 mg/ml protease (30 min at 37°C).
Centrifuge the solution at 13,000 rpm for 10 minutes.
Collect supernatant and test for plasmid concentration using Picogreen assay.
Calculate encapsulation ratio by dividing the encapsulated plasmid concentration with the initial loading of 0.5% (w/w).
Collect cell lysates from 2 million cells using lysis buffer.
Analyze total protein concentration in the collected lysate using BCA assay (Pierce).
Run 10 μg of total protein extract on pre-cast sodium dodecyl sulfate-polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis (SDS-PAGE) system at 135V for 90 minutes.
Transfer SDS-PAGE gel onto PVDF membrane by iBlot Dry Blotting System (Invitrogen).
Block the membrane with 5% non-fat milk in Tween-containing Tris buffer saline (TBS-t) for 1 hour at room temperature.
Incubate the membrane separately overnight at 4°C with 1:1,000 dilution of primary rabbit beta-actin antibodies and 1:1,000 dilution of primary rabbit EGFR antibodies.
Wash the membrane twice with TBS-t.
Incubate the membrane with 1:2,000 dilutions of secondary anti-rabbit horse-radish peroxidase-conjugated IgG in TBS-t for 1 hour at room temperature.
Rinse excess antibodies with TBS-t.
Rinse membranes with water.
Add 4 ml ECL substrate to the membranes.
Incubate the membranes with ECL substrate for 5 minutes.
Visualize chemiluminescent bands using a Kodak Digital X-ray Specimen (DXS) System.
Grow Panc-1 cells in 96-well plates at 10,000 cells per well in 200 μL of supplemented DMEM overnight.
Replace growth medium with serum-free media containing different concentrations of nanoparticles and 1 mg/ml PEI as a positive control.
Treat the cells with 200 μL of nanoparticles for 6 hours.
Add 20 μL MTS reagent to each well followed by 100 μL complete culture media.
Incubate treated cells at 37°C in 5% CO2 for 3 hours.
Measure absorbance of formazan product at 490 nm with a Biotek SynergyHT plate reader.
Conjugate Rhodamine B isothiocyanate (RBITC) on thiolated gelatin by reaction with amine group.
Dialyze and lyophilize the conjugated product to obtain RBITC-labeled thiolated gelatin.
Mix 25 μL of PicoGreen with 1 mg of plasmid for 1 minute.
Add labeled plasmids to the gelatin solution for nanoparticle preparation.
Grow Panc-1 cells in 6-well plates containing glass cover-slips at a density of 200,000 cells per well.
Treat each well with 2 mL of labeled nanoparticles (at a concentration of 1 mg/mL) in serum-free medium the next day after cell plating.
Replace the medium with culture medium containing 1 μg/mL of Hoest 33342 for 15 minutes incubation at room temperature at various time points from 15 minutes to 6 hours.
Add 2 mL of 4% paraformaldehyde solution to each well to fix cells.
Wash the cells twice with PBS.
Mount coverslips onto glass slides.
Use laser scanning confocal fluorescence microscopy to image fixed cells.
Encapsulate pEGFP-N1 plasmids into nanoparticles and suspend them in serum-free media at a concentration of 10 μg/mL for further treatments.
Grow Panc-1 cells overnight in a 6-well plate containing glass cover-slips at a density of 200,000 cells per well.
Treat each well with 2ml of pEGFP-N1 plasmids encapsulated nanoparticles.
Mix 20μg of plasmid DNA with 20μl Lipofectin cationic lipid transfection reagent for the positive control.
Incubate cells with different formulations for 6 hours.
Replace medium with fresh culture medium after 6-hour incubation.
Post-transfect cells for 24, 48, 72, and 96 hours.
Add 1μg/ml of Hoechst 33342 to the culture medium and incubate cells at room temperature for 15 minutes.
Mount coverslips onto glass slides after post-transfection.
Observe GFP expression in cells by fluorescence microscopy.
Acquire differential interference contrast (DIC) and fluorescence images using an Olympus BX61 microscope.
Process digital images with Image J software for analysis.
Quantitatively determine transfection efficiency via ELISA.
Grow Panc-1 cells overnight in 6-well plates with 200,000 cells per well.
Treat each well with 2 ml of pEGFP-N1 plasmids encapsulated nanoparticles.
Mix 20 μg of plasmids with 20 μl Lipofectin cationic lipid transfection reagent for positive control.
Incubate cells with different formulations for 6 hours.
Replace medium with culture medium after 6 hours incubation.
Post-incubate cells for 24, 48, 72 and 96 hours.
Collect cell lysates from each well post-transfection.
Analyze total protein concentration in cell lysates using BCA assay (Pierce).
Coat the plate with 100 μl of 1:1000 dilutions of monoclonal anti-GFP antibodies in each well.
Incubate the plate for 2 hours at room temperature.
Wash the plate four times with PBS-0.5% Tween-80.
Add 300 μl TBS blocking buffer into each well and incubate for 2 hours.
Wash the plate four times with PBS-0.5% (w/v) Tween-80 after blocking step.
Add 30 μg of proteins from each group into the plate and incubate overnight at 4°C.
Wash the plate four times with PBS-0.5% (w/v) Tween-80 before further analysis.
Dilute secondary anti-GFP antibodies to a 1:2400 ratio relative to alkaline phosphatase.
Add 100 μl of the diluted secondary anti-GFP antibody solution to each well.
Incubate for 1 hour at room temperature or as specified.
Wash each well with PBS-0.5% (w/v) Tween-80 four times.
Add 100 μl of alkaline phosphatase substrates to each well.
Incubate for 30 minutes to 1 hour at room temperature or as specified.
Measure the plate using a BioTek Synergy HT plate reader at 405 nm.
Express the GFP concentration in nanograms per milligram of total protein.
Encapsulate wt-p53 plasmids into nanoparticles and suspend them in serum-free media with a concentration equivalent to 10 μg plasmid per ml.
Grow Panc-1 cells overnight in 6-well plates at a density of 200,000 cells per well.
Treat each well with 2 ml of wt-p53 plasmids encapsulated nanoparticles.
Mix 20 μg of plasmids with 20 μl Lipofectin transfection reagent for the positive control group.
Incubate treated and untreated groups for 6 hours at room temperature or as specified.
Replace medium in each well with fresh culture medium after 6-hour incubation.
Post-incubate cells for 48 hours at 37°C in a CO2 incubator.
Extract mRNA from each well using the High Pure RNA isolation kit (Roche).
Measure extracted RNA concentration using a Nanodrop 2000 (Thermo Scientific).
Grow Panc-1 cells overnight in 6-well plates with 200,000 cells per well.
Treat each well with 2 ml of wt-p53 plasmid encapsulated nanoparticles suspended in serum-free media at a concentration equivalent to 10 μg plasmids per ml.
Mix 20 μg of plasmids with 20 μl Lipofectin and use as positive control, while untreated cells serve as negative control.
Incubate cells with different formulations for 6 hours.
Replace medium with culture medium after initial incubation.
Post-incubate cells for 24, 48, 72, and 96 hours.
Use iCys Research Imaging Cytometer from CompuCyte (Westwood, MA) to analyze and compare apoptosis levels after treatment.
Record fluorescence microscopic image intensities of all colors versus counts and calculate percentages for different populations.
Calculate apoptotic cell fold changes compared to the negative control with no treatment.
Use Apo-ONE Homogeneous Caspase-3/7 Assay kit (Promega, Madison, WI) to examine pro-apoptotic activity after transfection of wt-p53 plasmid.
Treat cells post-transfection with rhodamine 110, Z-DEVD-R110 for up to 18 hours.
Measure the plate with BioTek Synergy HT plate reader for fluorescence at 490/520 nm.
Synthesis and characterization of EGFR targeted nanoparticles.
Prepare nanoparticles by desolvation method.
Characterize particle size and zeta potential of the synthesized nanoparticles.
Determine average size and surface charge for particles prepared from thiolated gelatins with different degrees of thiolation.
Observe sizes, surface morphology, and spherical shape of nanoparticles using SEM analysis.
Compare SEM results with Zetasizer results.
Measure DNA loading efficiencies in gelatin nanoparticles and thiolated gelatin nanoparticles.
Analyze two human pancreatic adenocarcinoma cell lines (Panc-1 and Capan-1) by western blot for EGFR expression.
Use human ovarian adenocarcinoma (SKOV3) cells as positive control.
Use murine fibroblast (NIH-3T3) cells as negative control.
Evaluate cellular interaction of nanoparticles using cytotoxicity assays after treatment with nanoparticles.
Conduct studies with 1 mg/ml nanoparticle concentration.
Label EGFR-targeting peptide and receptor-mediated endocytotic uptake components with different fluorescence for visualization.
Use laser scanning confocal fluorescence microscopy to take images at various time points, from 15 minutes to 6 hours.
Compare the images of different formulations to analyze nanoparticle uptake and trafficking in cells.
Confirm fast uptake and plasmid release within 30 minutes for peptide-conjugated gelatin nanoparticles.
Prove that EGFR peptide-conjugated nanoparticles undergo facilitated endocytosis with rapid interaction between specific peptides and receptors on cell surfaces.
Compare the rate of uptake to other nanoparticles undergoing non-specific endocytosis.
Extract wild-type p53 plasmids pORF-hp53 with EF-1α/HTLV hybrid promoter from E. coli.
Encapsulate the extracted plasmids into nanoparticles.
Treat Panc-1 cells with the particles for 6 hours.
Post-transfect Panc-1 cells for additional 24, 48, 72, and 96 hours.
Extract mRNA from Panc-1 cells after 48 hours post-transfection.
Use extracted mRNA for RT-PCR analysis.
Evaluate RT-PCR products with gel electrophoresis.
Analyze bands using ImageJ software.
